From fea3fdf975dd9f3e5248afaab8fe023db313f005 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
Date: Tue, 14 Dec 2021 09:41:26 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] drm/ast: potential dereference of null pointer

The return value of kzalloc() needs to be checked.
To avoid use of null pointer '&ast_state->base' in case of the
failure of alloc.

Fixes: f0adbc382b8b ("drm/ast: Allocate initial CRTC state of the correct size")
Signed-off-by: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20211214014126.2211535-1-jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn

diff --git a/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c b/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c
index 1e30eaeb0e1b..d5c98f79d58d 100644
--- a/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c
+++ b/drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c
@@ -1121,7 +1121,10 @@ static void ast_crtc_reset(struct drm_crtc *crtc)
 	if (crtc->state)
 		crtc->funcs->atomic_destroy_state(crtc, crtc->state);
 
-	__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
+	if (ast_state)
+		__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
+	else
+		__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, NULL);
 }
 
 static struct drm_crtc_state *
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/gpu/drm/ast/ast_mode.c`**
- The function `ast_crtc_reset` was modified to include a null pointer check for `ast_state` before dereferencing it.
- If `ast_state` is not null, it calls `__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base)`.
- If `ast_state` is null, it calls `__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, NULL)` instead.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a potential null pointer dereference issue that could occur if the allocation of `ast_state` fails. By checking if `ast_state` is null before using it, the patch prevents the program from attempting to access `&ast_state->base`, which would lead to undefined behavior. This change is directly related to the previous commit that allocated the initial CRTC state, ensuring that the code remains robust against allocation failures.

Here is the commit message:
drm/ast: potential dereference of null pointer

The return value of kzalloc() needs to be checked.
To avoid use of null pointer '&ast_state->base' in case of the
failure of alloc.

Fixes: f0adbc382b8b ("drm/ast: Allocate initial CRTC state of the correct size")
Signed-off-by: Jiasheng Jiang <jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn>
Signed-off-by: Thomas Zimmermann <tzimmermann@suse.de>
Link: https://patchwork.freedesktop.org/patch/msgid/20211214014126.2211535-1-jiasheng@iscas.ac.cn

Here is the root cause:
The bug arises from the lack of a null pointer check after the allocation of `ast_state`, which is done using `kzalloc()`. If the allocation fails, `ast_state` would be null, and dereferencing it to access `&ast_state->base` would lead to a potential null pointer dereference, causing a crash or undefined behavior.

Here is the patch:
 
 static void ast_crtc_reset(struct drm_crtc *crtc)
 {
 	struct ast_crtc_state *ast_state =
 		kzalloc(sizeof(*ast_state), GFP_KERNEL);
 
 	if (crtc->state)
 		crtc->funcs->atomic_destroy_state(crtc, crtc->state);
 
-	__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
+	if (ast_state)
+		__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
+	else
+		__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, NULL);
 }

Root cause:
The bug arises from the lack of a null pointer check after the allocation of `ast_state`, which is done using `kzalloc()`. If the allocation fails, `ast_state` would be null, and dereferencing it to access `&ast_state->base` would lead to a potential null pointer dereference, causing a crash or undefined behavior.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
struct ast_crtc_state *ast_state = kzalloc(sizeof(*ast_state), GFP_KERNEL);
__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because there is no check to see if `ast_state` is null after the call to `kzalloc()`. If the memory allocation fails, `ast_state` will be null, and dereferencing it to access `&ast_state->base` will lead to a null pointer dereference, resulting in a crash or undefined behavior.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (ast_state)
    __drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, &ast_state->base);
else
    __drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, NULL);
```
Reason:
The fix introduces a null pointer check for `ast_state` before dereferencing it. If `ast_state` is null, the code safely calls `__drm_atomic_helper_crtc_reset(crtc, NULL)`, preventing a null pointer dereference and ensuring that the function behaves correctly even when memory allocation fails.
